description: Believes the base case always returns 0 (or that 'base' means zero) instead of the value that keeps the maths correct.
remediation: Trace factorial(3) by hand on paper; show that returning 0 makes every result 0. Contrast sum-recursion (base 0) with product-recursion (base 1).

description: Believes recursion with a base case can still run forever, or does not see what makes the calls stop.
remediation: Step through a call stack diagram and mark the exact call where the base case fires and the stack unwinds.

description: Thinks a base case returns nothing/None rather than a value that is passed back up.
remediation: Have the learner annotate what each frame returns to its caller on a worked example.

description: Chooses 'Error' whenever code looks unfamiliar; reads syntax rather than behaviour.
remediation: Run the code in a REPL together and predict-then-check before explaining.

description: Assumes Python quietly returns a default value when a base case is missing.
remediation: Run a base-case-free function and read the RecursionError traceback.

description: Does not know that each call uses stack space, so thinks infinite recursion just 'keeps going'.
remediation: Draw stack frames growing until the limit; show sys.getrecursionlimit().

description: Mixes up heap memory exhaustion with call-stack depth limits.
remediation: Contrast a huge list (MemoryError) with deep recursion (RecursionError).

description: Thinks OverflowError (numbers too big) is what stack overflow means.
remediation: Compare the two error names and triggers side by side in a REPL.

description: Thinks the result is just the last call's value, not the values combined on the way back up.
remediation: Expand f(3) = 3 + f(2) = 3 + (2 + f(1)) ... line by line until it collapses to a number.

description: Treats recursion as needing a loop; confuses repetition mechanisms.
remediation: Rewrite the same task as a loop and as recursion; show the base case plays the role of the loop condition.

description: Believes termination needs a global counter instead of a condition on the argument.
remediation: Show a function that shrinks its argument toward the base case with no global state.

description: Differentiates x^n but forgets to reduce the exponent.
remediation: Practise d/dx x^n = n·x^(n-1) with a table of small cases.

description: Drops the exponent as a multiplier when differentiating.
remediation: Compare slopes numerically to show the n factor.
